title: Greek Yogurt vs Sour Cream: Protein, Fat, and Calories

seo.title: Greek Yogurt vs Sour Cream: Nutrition
seo.meta_description: Plain Greek yogurt often has about 9–10 g of protein per 100 g versus roughly 2–3 g in sour cream, and low-fat versions can be far lower in calories.
seo.search_intent: Compare Greek yogurt and sour cream by protein, fat, calories, and cooking behavior.

excerpt: Plain Greek yogurt commonly delivers about 9–10 g of protein per 100 g compared with roughly 2–3 g in full-fat sour cream. Nonfat or low-fat Greek yogurt also cuts the fat and calorie load sharply.
content_html:
Greek yogurt and sour cream can look almost interchangeable on a baked potato, but the nutrition gap is substantial. Plain Greek yogurt commonly provides about 9–10 g of protein per 100 g, versus roughly 2–3 g in full-fat sour cream.

Greek yogurt is much more protein-dense

Straining removes whey and concentrates milk proteins, which is why Greek yogurt carries more protein than standard cultured cream. That matters when the serving is more than a garnish.

Fat depends on the yogurt you buy

Nonfat Greek yogurt contains almost no fat; whole-milk Greek yogurt can contain roughly 5–10 g per 100 g. Traditional sour cream is typically around 18–20 g of fat per 100 g.

The calorie difference follows

Nonfat Greek yogurt is often around 55–65 calories per 100 g, with whole-milk versions closer to 100–130. Full-fat sour cream commonly approaches 190–210 calories per 100 g. Check the label because styles vary.

They do not behave identically under heat

Greek yogurt works well in dips, dressings, tacos, and baked-potato toppings. In hot sauces, low-fat yogurt is more prone to curdling, so gentle heat and adding it near the end help.

The practical trade-off

Choose Greek yogurt when protein and lower fat matter; choose sour cream when its richer fat-driven texture is the point of the dish.

faq.question: Which has more protein, Greek yogurt or sour cream?
faq.answer: Greek yogurt, usually by a wide margin: roughly 9–10 g/100 g versus about 2–3 g/100 g.

faq.question: Can Greek yogurt replace sour cream?
faq.answer: Often in dips and toppings. Use gentle heat in cooked sauces because low-fat yogurt can curdle.

faq.question: Which has fewer calories?
faq.answer: Greek yogurt usually does, especially nonfat or low-fat versions.
